newsitem.title: USA: Stars' "healer" arrested for not filing tax returns.
newsitem.headline: Stars' "healer" arrested for not filing tax returns.

text.p: A man who claims royalty, celebrities and politicans have asked him for healing was arrested on Thursday on charges of failing to file tax returns for three years, prosecutors said.

Ze'ev Kolman, 58, a well-known practitioner of alternative medicine who lives in a condo near New York's Plaza Hotel, failed to file returns on $1 million in personal income, Manhattan District Attorney Robert Morgenthau said.

Prosecutors allege he did not file returns for three years starting in 1993, and owes more than $90,000 in personal income taxes and another $50,000 in unincorporated city business taxes for his practice, Bio-Energetic Healing - The Life Force.
He faces up to four years in prison and hefty fines if convicted.

According to a book that delves into Kolman's healing powers, he claims to have helped such Hollywood stars as Melanie Griffith, Don Johnson, Barbra Streisand, Raquel Welch, Goldie Hawn and Robert Wagner.
He also boasts of helping physicans, psychologists and "some of Europe's royal families."

But when asked by reporters at Kolman's arraignment on Thursday why some celebrities denied ever knowing him, his defence lawyer, Andrew Rendares, said: "Lots of these celebrities don't want to admit they go to unconventional sources rather than conventional doctors."
Yet the book jacket has a ringing endorsement by singer Carly Simon, who said Kolman is "an exceptionally gifted and loving person devoted to healing the body, mind and soul."
Actor Robert Wagner also gave Kolman a glowing report in the book: "I am very much impressed with Ze'ev Kolman's abilities as a healer."
Kolman claims he "has devoted his life to healing the sick with his extraordinary gift," according to his book.
Kolman, an Israeli citizen, had to surrender his passport after pleading not guilty at his arraignment. He was released on his own recognisance.
